set.body:
Found in the first-level contract v1 review (bd-01M31KPY7EK45HKWB9TJS1VFWJ, candidate f279c76b). It was reproduced independently by two fresh-context reviewers.

Defect: canonical identity strings are built by interpolating Doubles and case-class toString. Scala.js prints integral Doubles without ".0", so the same model produces different IDs, and different digests, on the JVM and JS.

Root cause and propagation:
- modules/hrf/shared/src/main/scala/scalafim/fmri/hrf/HrfDescriptor.scala:235 canonicalId interpolates span=${span.value} and the toString of params, derivative and integration.
- From there: BasisElement.infer (Basis.scala:145-146) -> BasisElementId -> BasisElementRef.canonical element= (design DesignSchema.scala:158) -> StructuralColumnOrigin.Event.canonical -> StructuralColumn.fromOrigin (DesignSchema.scala:295) -> native ColumnId.
- Observed in column 0 of a two-run FmriModelBuilder design:
  - JVM: span=24.0 ... SpmgParams(5.0,15.0,0.008333333333333333)
  - JS: span=24 ... SpmgParams(5,15,0.008333333333333333)
- The drift column ID is identical on both platforms. Event and basis columns diverge.
- DesignFingerprint also diverges on the single-run design: DesignAudit.canonical renders rank-preview doubles with toString. JVM design-schema/v1:ac3f77b22441f613 vs JS design-schema/v1:77fb13c7f35bf7a9 (tolerance 2.842170943040401E-14 vs e-14).

Related latent bugs:
- Basis.scala:82 FirBin.stableLabel interpolates Double from/until, which will diverge for FIR designs.
- Basis.scala:82-89 uses s"...${index}%02d" without the f interpolator, so a literal %02d ends up in IDs, e.g. basis-1%2502d. This is stable across platforms but wrong.

Required fix:
- Canonical identity must use a platform-independent, exact rendering: e.g. Double bits as a hex long, or a canonical shortest-roundtrip decimal implemented in shared code. Never toString of a Double or a case class.
- Add a shared JVM+JS golden test pinning the IDs and fingerprints for single-run, two-run and FIR designs.
- Changing IDs is a breaking identity change, so audit persisted artifacts and fixtures that embed these IDs.

Consumer impact: contract v1 pins the design and readout digests per platform, with a tripwire that fails once the platforms converge (ResponseSourceBinderSuite two-run golden).
set.title: HRF/design structural IDs differ between JVM and Scala.js (Double/case-class toString in canonical identity)
